pr_title: base: make TestValidateAddrs work without a network connection
pr_body:
Looking up an invalid host name may result in a different error depending on whether the test has access to a network connection or not. This patch modifies the test to catch that.

Fixes: #109052

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/110069)

issue_context.title: pkg/base: base_test fails if no network access
issue_context.body:
Looks like `TestValidateAddrs/23/{nonexistent.example.com:26257_____}` fails.

```
    addr_validation_test.go:169: expected error "no such host", got invalid --listen-addr: lookup nonexistent.example.com on 169.254.169.254:53: dial udp 169.254.169.254:53: connect: network is unreachable
```

Epic: CRDB-8308

Jira issue: CRDB-30751
comments: The ownership here may be a bit fuzzy. Tagging @knz since this test case apparently originates from him.

Yes that test needs access to a valid dns resolver because it checks for resolution error.

(Note how it uses example.com to be guaranteed to get an error)

It's possible to use a local dns server with no internet access as long as it responds with errors to those queries.

The test is a unit test, so it shouldn't have a dependency on random stuff from the internet.

> It's possible to use a local dns server with no internet access

If you update the test to do so, then that seems fine -- until that point it seems the test should be skipped? Or there should be an opt-in configuration to run "integration-style tests".

You can also mock out the lookup. Or delete the sub-test -- I wonder if it actually provides any value, or if it's possible for it to fail in a way that is meaningful and representative of an actual bug. Of course the lookup for a non-existent domain will fail -- what do we get from checking?

The test is checking the text of the error encountered so that it matches what we have in documentation. I don't find it superfluous.

I welcome your suggestions on how to mock this. (I am also not the owner of this code currently so my attention here will be best effort. Ask @nkodali if there's any urgency)

> I welcome your suggestions on how to mock this.

Instead of directly using `net.Resolver`, use a mock object behind an interface. That object needs `LookupPort` and `LookupIPAddr` methods. For the production case, you would just use the `DefaultResolver`. For testing, use a fake object that doesn't do actual DNS lookups. Functions in `net` like `SplitHostPort` would help with implementation. In the error case being discussed, you just need to make sure `LookupIPAddr` returns an error `"no such host"`, which is exactly what the [actual implementation does](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/master:src/net/net.go;l=617?q=%22no%20such%20host%22&ss=go%2Fgo).

review_comments:
have you even checked with @rickystewart whether this was a good fix?
I fear with this code that `noSuchHostErr("foo") == noSuchHostErr("bar")` and so the test below is testing something unrelated.

> have you even checked with @rickystewart whether this was a good fix?

I haven't; @rickystewart thoughts?

> I fear with this code that `noSuchHostErr("foo") == noSuchHostErr("bar")` and so the test below is testing something unrelated.

`noSuchHostErr("foo") != noSuchHostErr("bar")` -- the host's name is printed in the error, which is actually why I had to pass the host name as a parameter. The error's something like "<hostname> no such host" IIRC.

The fix seems to work inasmuch as it fixes the test. It works since we expect to get "some" error, whatever it is, and we just check whether it matches up to the expected error.

Note that this test will run in an environment without network access. To me this means the way the test is written is pretty misleading -- the IP lookup is going to fail in CI, whether the domain we're looking up is example.com or google.com or whatever. This also means that the "test" in CI is going to differ from the "test" as people run it on their local machines -- they'll be performing different `assert`s.

IMO it is more correct to [follow the advice I gave](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/109052#issuecomment-1686600283) and mock the network lookup in a unit test: it is a *unit test*, so we shouldn't have a dependency on the network, and the test should be written such that we don't do useless network lookups that are guaranteed to fail.

For this, all I care about is whether the test is or is not failing, so I think it's fine as written.
